title: A command palette
description:
Code editors open a **command palette** with Ctrl+Shift+P: type a few letters of any command and it appears at the top. Write the search behind one, for the command table from lesson 4.01's practice.

```cpp
class Palette
{
public:
    void add(const std::string& name);                   // "File/Save Level"
    void ran(const std::string& name);                   // the user ran this command (it becomes the most recent)
    int score(const std::string& query, const std::string& name) const;   // -1 when it does not match
    std::vector<std::string> search(const std::string& query, std::size_t limit) const;
};
```

**Matching and scoring** (`score`), ignoring upper and lower case:

- Every character of the query must appear in the name **in order** (not necessarily next to each other): `"svl"` matches `"File/Save Level"`. Spaces in the query are ignored.
- Match each query character at the **earliest** position after the previous match (left to right, no backtracking). If some character cannot be found, the score is `-1`.
- Each matched character scores **1**, plus **5** if it comes right after the previous matched character, plus **8** if it is at the **start of a word**: the first character of the name, a character after a space, `/`, `_` or `-`, or an upper-case letter right after a lower-case one (in the original spelling: `"saveLevel"`, the `L`).
- An empty query (or only spaces) scores 0 for every name.

**Searching** (`search`): the names with a score of 0 or more, best first; ties go to the more **recently run** command (commands never run come after those that were); then alphabetical. Return at most `limit` names.

```
add "File/Save Level", "File/Save As", "View/Show Stats", "Edit/Select All"
score("sl", "File/Save Level") = (1 + 8) + (1 + 8) = 18      (S and L both start words)
score("sl", "Edit/Select All") = (1 + 8) + 1 = 10                (the l of Select follows an unmatched e: no bonus)
```
hints: Write `wordStart(name, i)` first, then `score` as one loop over the query characters that remembers where the previous match was.
requirements: Matching is a case-insensitive, in-order subsequence; spaces in the query are ignored.
The score follows the rules exactly, including word starts in camelCase.
Results are ordered by score, then recency, then name, and limited.
An empty query lists every command, most recent first.
stretch: Highlight the matched characters: return their positions as well, and draw them in the accent colour with `ImGui::TextColored` pieces on one line.
